prompt:
Answer in the client's language: choose it from the request's `Accept-Language` header (`ko` or `en`, honoring q-values and region tags such as `ko-KR`; anything else falls back to `LARDER_LANG`), and give every error code a Korean message.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Errors now answer in `ko` or `en` based on `Accept-Language` (q-values and region tags honored), falling back to `LARDER_LANG`, and every error code has a Korean message. `npm test` (26 tests) and `npm run lint` pass; I checked the new behavior with throwaway scripts and added no tests, since the task didn't ask for them. Three additions you might not assume: `internal` is now in `CODES` with its own translated message instead of hard-coded English; `bad_request` reasons and `order_state` state/action words are translated too, so Korean messages aren't half English; and dynamic reasons became templates, with English text unchanged. An unsupported tag is skipped, so `fr, ko;q=0.3` picks `ko`, and a malformed q-value drops that entry. Only error messages are localized: outbox notices, CSV exports and stored data such as item names and units stay as they are.

check.why: language negotiation and every message in Korean
